correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the sequence-b definitions and handles all quantifiers. A mixed-shore color class is proved to be exactly one deleted matched pair. For \(q\ge3\) it cannot contain enough CDVs. For \(q=2\), two CDVs in one mixed pair force every other color onto both shores, hence every color class is a deleted pair and the graph must be the excluded balanced full-matching crown. If all classes are shore-pure, \(k\ge3\) forces two colors on one shore, so those classes have no CDV. The bipartition coloring supplies the matching lower bound for \(q\le m\); connectedness makes it the only two-coloring, so \(q>m\) is impossible. The finite checker corroborates but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies an infinite, canonical perturbation family for every constant CDV requirement \(q\ge2\), not a finite parameter slice. The mixed-pair propagation lemma identifies a sharp structural obstruction explaining why every non-crown matching deletion has only the two-color realization. This supplies a natural exact benchmark for the newly introduced spectrum.
